True Statement: Blood is a special connective tissue consisting of a fluid matrix, plasma, and formed elements.

Reason: Blood is a connective tissue because its cells (formed elements) are suspended in a ground substance (plasma), as in other connective tissues.

True Statement: Plasma is a straw coloured, viscous fluid constituting nearly 55 per cent of the blood.

Reason: Plasma constitutes 55% of blood; it is the liquid phase that carries nutrients, hormones and waste products.

True Statement: 90-92 per cent of plasma is water and proteins contribute 6-8 per cent of it.

True Statement: Fibrinogen, globulins and albumins are the major proteins of plasma.
False 1: Fibrinogen, globulins and haemoglobin are the major proteins of plasma.
FIB 1: ___, globulins and albumins are the major proteins of plasma.

FIB 3: Fibrinogen, globulins and albumins are the major ___ of plasma.
Reason: Fibrinogen, globulins and albumins serve different functions: fibrinogen for clotting, globulins for immunity, albumins for osmotic balance.

True Statement: Fibrinogens are needed for clotting or coagulation of blood.
False 1: Globulins are needed for clotting or coagulation of blood.
False 2: Fibrinogens are needed for the osmotic balance of blood.
FIB 1: ___ are needed for clotting or coagulation of blood.
FIB 2: Fibrinogens are needed for ___ or coagulation of blood.
FIB 3: Fibrinogens are needed for clotting or ___ of blood.
Reason: Fibrinogen is converted to fibrin during clotting; fibrin threads form the meshwork that traps blood cells to form a clot.

True Statement: Globulins are primarily involved in defense mechanisms of the body.
False 1: Albumins are primarily involved in defense mechanisms of the body.
False 2: Fibrinogens are primarily involved in defense mechanisms of the body.

FIB 2: Globulins are primarily involved in ___ mechanisms of the body.
FIB 3: Globulins are primarily involved in defense ___ of the body.
Reason: Globulins include immunoglobulins (antibodies) and complement proteins; they are central to humoral immunity.

True Statement: Albumins help in osmotic balance.
False 1: Globulins help in osmotic balance.
False 2: Albumins help in blood clotting.
FIB 1: ___ help in osmotic balance.
FIB 2: Albumins help in ___ balance.
FIB 3: Albumins help in osmotic ___.
Reason: Albumin is the most abundant plasma protein; its high concentration creates oncotic (colloidal osmotic) pressure that retains water in the blood vessels.

True Statement: Plasma also contains small amounts of minerals like Na⁺, Ca⁺⁺, Mg⁺⁺, HCO₃⁻, Cl⁻, etc.

True Statement: Factors for coagulation or clotting of blood are present in the plasma in an inactive form.

True Statement: Plasma without the clotting factors is called serum.

True Statement: Erythrocytes, leucocytes and platelets are collectively called formed elements and they constitute nearly 45 per cent of the blood.

Reason: Formed elements are the cellular components; they constitute 45% of blood (haematocrit) and include RBCs, WBCs and platelets.

True Statement: A healthy adult man has, on an average, 5 millions to 5.5 millions of RBCs mm⁻³ of blood.

Reason: RBC count (5–5.5 million mm⁻³) is much higher than WBC count because oxygen delivery requires a very high concentration of haemoglobin.

True Statement: RBCs are formed in the red bone marrow in adults.
False 1: RBCs are formed in the yellow bone marrow in adults.

Reason: Red bone marrow contains haematopoietic stem cells; yellow marrow is fat-storing and does not produce RBCs in normal adults.

True Statement: RBCs are devoid of nucleus in most mammals and are biconcave in shape.
False 1: RBCs are nucleated in most mammals and are biconcave in shape.
False 2: RBCs are devoid of nucleus in most mammals and are biconvex in shape.

True Statement: RBCs have a red coloured, iron containing complex protein called haemoglobin.
False 1: RBCs have a red coloured, copper containing complex protein called haemoglobin.
False 2: WBCs have a red coloured, iron containing complex protein called haemoglobin.

FIB 2: RBCs have a red coloured, iron containing complex ___ called haemoglobin.
FIB 3: RBCs have a red coloured, iron containing complex protein called ___.
Reason: Haem iron (Fe²⁺) binds O₂ reversibly; the globin protein stabilises the haem and modulates O₂ affinity.

True Statement: A healthy individual has 12-16 gms of haemoglobin in every 100 ml of blood.

Reason: 12–16 g/100 mL is the normal range; values below 12 g (anaemia) impair O₂ delivery; values above 16 g may indicate polycythaemia.

True Statement: RBCs have an average life span of 120 days after which they are destroyed in the spleen (graveyard of RBCs).
False 1: RBCs have an average life span of 60 days after which they are destroyed in the spleen.
False 2: RBCs have an average life span of 120 days after which they are destroyed in the liver.

True Statement: Leucocytes are colourless due to the lack of haemoglobin.
False 1: Leucocytes are colourless due to the lack of plasma proteins.
False 2: Erythrocytes are colourless due to the lack of haemoglobin.

FIB 3: Leucocytes are colourless due to the lack of ___.
Reason: WBCs lack haemoglobin (the red pigment of RBCs); they contain no haem-iron and have colourless cytoplasm.

True Statement: Leucocytes are nucleated and average 6000-8000 mm⁻³ of blood.
False 1: Leucocytes are nucleated and average 5 millions to 5.5 millions mm⁻³ of blood.
False 2: Leucocytes are non-nucleated and average 6000-8000 mm⁻³ of blood.
FIB 1: ___ are nucleated and average 6000-8000 mm⁻³ of blood.
FIB 2: Leucocytes are nucleated and ___ 6000-8000 mm⁻³ of blood.
FIB 3: Leucocytes are nucleated and average ___ mm⁻³ of blood.
Reason: WBCs are nucleated (unlike mammalian RBCs) because they need to transcribe genes for immune functions; their lower count (6,000–8,000) reflects surveillance, not bulk transport.

True Statement: Neutrophils, eosinophils and basophils are different types of granulocytes, while lymphocytes and monocytes are the agranulocytes.
False 1: Neutrophils, eosinophils and lymphocytes are different types of granulocytes, while basophils and monocytes are the agranulocytes.
False 2: Neutrophils, eosinophils and basophils are different types of agranulocytes, while lymphocytes and monocytes are the granulocytes.

Reason: Granulocytes have visible cytoplasmic granules; agranulocytes (lymphocytes, monocytes) have no such granules under light microscopy.

True Statement: Neutrophils are the most abundant cells (60-65 per cent) of the total WBCs and basophils are the least (0.5-1 per cent).
False 1: Lymphocytes are the most abundant cells (60-65 per cent) of the total WBCs.
False 2: Neutrophils are the most abundant cells (60-65 per cent) of the total WBCs and eosinophils are the least (0.5-1 per cent).

FIB 3: Neutrophils are the most abundant cells (60-65 per cent) of the total WBCs and basophils are the least (___ per cent).
Reason: Neutrophils are first responders (60–65%) because of their abundance and rapid phagocytic ability; basophils are rare (0.5–1%) because only small amounts of histamine-releasing cells are needed.

True Statement: Neutrophils and monocytes (6-8 per cent) are phagocytic cells which destroy foreign organisms entering the body.
False 1: Lymphocytes and monocytes are phagocytic cells which destroy foreign organisms entering the body.
False 2: Neutrophils and eosinophils are phagocytic cells which destroy foreign organisms entering the body.

FIB 2: Neutrophils and monocytes (___ per cent) are phagocytic cells which destroy foreign organisms entering the body.
FIB 3: Neutrophils and monocytes (6-8 per cent) are ___ cells which destroy foreign organisms entering the body.
Reason: Neutrophils and monocytes engulf pathogens by phagocytosis; monocytes can differentiate into macrophages in tissues for sustained phagocytosis.

True Statement: Basophils secrete histamine, serotonin, heparin, etc., and are involved in inflammatory reactions.

FIB 2: Basophils secrete histamine, serotonin, heparin, etc., and are involved in ___ reactions.
FIB 3: Basophils secrete histamine, serotonin, heparin, etc., and are involved in inflammatory ___.
Reason: Basophil granules contain pre-formed mediators (histamine, heparin, serotonin) released rapidly during allergic and inflammatory responses.

True Statement: Eosinophils (2-3 per cent) resist infections and are also associated with allergic reactions.

FIB 3: Eosinophils (2-3 per cent) resist infections and are also ___ with allergic reactions.
Reason: Eosinophils release toxic proteins against parasites and modulate allergic reactions; they contain major basic protein that damages parasite cuticles.

True Statement: Lymphocytes (20-25 per cent) are of two major types – 'B' and 'T' forms; both are responsible for immune responses of the body.
False 1: Monocytes (20-25 per cent) are of two major types – 'B' and 'T' forms; both are responsible for immune responses of the body.

True Statement: Platelets (thrombocytes) are cell fragments produced from megakaryocytes (special cells in the bone marrow).

True Statement: Blood normally contains 1,500,00-3,500,00 platelets mm⁻³.

True Statement: ABO grouping is based on the presence or absence of two surface antigens on the RBCs, namely A and B.

True Statement: The Rh antigen is similar to one present in Rhesus monkeys and is observed on the surface of RBCs of nearly 80 per cent of humans.

True Statement: An Rh-ve person, if exposed to Rh+ve blood, will form specific antibodies against the Rh antigens.

Reason: In the second Rh+ve pregnancy, maternal anti-Rh IgG (formed after the first delivery) crosses the placenta and destroys foetal RBCs → erythroblastosis foetalis.

True Statement: Erythroblastosis foetalis can be avoided by administering anti-Rh antibodies to the mother immediately after the delivery of the first child.

True Statement: Fibrins are formed by the conversion of inactive fibrinogens in the plasma by the enzyme thrombin.

True Statement: Thrombins are formed from another inactive substance present in the plasma called prothrombin.

True Statement: An enzyme complex, thrombokinase, is required to convert prothrombin to thrombin.

Reason: Thrombokinase is an enzyme complex (factor Xa + Va) that activates prothrombin; it forms only when the coagulation cascade is triggered by injury.

True Statement: Calcium ions play a very important role in blood clotting.

Reason: Ca²⁺ ions are essential cofactors for multiple steps in the coagulation cascade; chelating Ca²⁺ (with citrate) prevents clotting in stored blood.

True Statement: As blood passes through capillaries in tissues, some water and small water-soluble substances move out into spaces between cells, leaving the larger proteins and most formed elements in the blood vessels.

True Statement: The fluid released from blood capillaries into tissue spaces is called the interstitial fluid or tissue fluid.
